question: In ESOI, intents are meaningful containers of a set of specifications. For human understanding, they serve as a personal category of interest or relate to a tangible container such as an organization.
What is a specific phrase which distinguishes the topic of the intent from other intents?
What is this intent manifesting in present tense? e.g. "I am ..." or "The world is ..." Any subject and verb can be used.
What are potentials inspired by this intent?

A general category like "parenting" or "career." An intent is also not an organization itself, rather the container of specification that clarifies why the organization exists (as a solution and implementation within an intent). In this example, different versions of the same organization can be documented as separate alternative implementations.
A description of what motivated the intent. A challenge, difficulty, or description of how an ideal is not reached.
What is the problem?
Who or what type of person has the problem?
Why does this problem matter?
Why is the problem hard to resolve?
What solutions or workarounds already attempt to address the problem?
A decision, task, recommendation, or component, but all of these can *have* problems.
Ideals that oppose at least one aspect of the problem, Solutions that would solve at least one aspect of the problem
A strategic definition of how one or more problems can be addressed to fulfill the intent.
What's a name that describes the type of solution it is?
What is the solution's unique value proposition, which justifies its existence? (Consider how it differs from other solutions, without explicitly stating anything about other solutions)
An inspiring sentence which clarifies the niche of utility that the solution serves without enumerating use cases. Start with a verb and name who or what it serves where relevant.

An inspiring sentence which clarifies how the solution solves problems, which applies to every implementation. This is also the solution's human-readable strategy statement. Start with a verb and name no actor (worded like a responsibility).
What type of use cases is the solution intentionally avoiding, which exclusions aren't otherwise apparent or typical? (Don't explicitly name other solutions that aren't in scope)

What are the solution's priorities in order? Every solution specifies at least one. Each milestone is a value of one or more metrics, which doesn't have to be the authoritative metric directly but it should relate to it. End condition (optional): Condition for the milestone to no longer be a priority (date or other circumstance), at which point it's archived. Met: Whether the milestone has been reached, and when. Target completion time (optional): Planned completion date and time (which other dependent milestones may rely on). May be a date or a specific minute of a date where precision is needed.

What knowledge informs the solution's definition or implementations? This can be a list of many items, including chosen assumptions, best guesses, evidence, theories, or perspectives which inform the solution or its implementations.
What would indicate the solution is successful?

What classifications may be necessary to avoid risk? Risk Addressed: Every tag should name what risk it mitigates, which are linked problems, whether from the same intent as the solution or from other intents (such as R1-R4 below which are problems defined for ESOI). Tags are not problems themselves; they help mitigate structural problems such as through tagging topics or types of technology used. Note: Possible risks (structural problems): R1 (duplication): Adding a new solution that duplicates an existing one. R2 (opportunity): Not leveraging the benefits of an existing solution, such as partial overlap of purpose. R3 (dependency): Not being aware of solutions that need to change definition or implementation due to something else changing. R4 (mistake): Using a solution when it should not be for the particular use case.

Other information on when and how to use the solution
Fully functional code or solution, but it can be an abstract class, template, or routing which a separate structure solution network defines.
Implementations that build what the solution defines, Metrics that define and implement the solution's measures of success, Problems the solution addresses.
The built structure which carries out its associated solution; also known as an alternative.
What's a name that distinguishes this implementation from other alternatives?

What is the implementation's unique value proposition, to achieve the purpose of its solution? (Consider how it differs from other existing or potential alternatives, without explicitly stating anything about other implementations)
Advantages
Disadvantages
Solutions that the implementation uses. Note: Ideally the ESOI framework used enables automatic dependency awareness.
What end users of the relevant solution directly interact with. The solution provides an interface on top of the implementation. A structure solution defines how solutions will define interfaces.
A definition of the future state implied by the intent, in a particular dimension or aspect.
What's a combined noun with adjective that represents the ideal's direction of interest?
What does this ideal ask for?
Describe what it would be like to experience this ideal.
How would you know this ideal is reached?
A practical metric or solution, or technology.
Problems the ideal opposes.

A practical way to measure the distance between the implementations of a solution and an ideal which the solution was defined to achieve. Alternative implementations are compared via metrics. Consequently, every solution has only one authoritative metric, which can be a combination of multiple metrics or factors with weights that reflect the solution's ideals and purpose. Note: Metrics can also be solutions, as metrics themselves may be refined over time with alternative implementations (including dataset versions).
What's a name that clarifies what is being measured?

A statement of what the metric ensures, specifically and comprehensively yet simply stated. This statement does not need to enumerate its current implementation, rather it encapsulates an intention to measure.
What is recorded as the metric to compare implementations?
What can the metric not see, or what could it reward wrongly?
